rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; p560 p. 39, Deduction Worksheet for Self-Employed, Step 1: "Enter your net profit from Schedule C (Form 1040), line 31; Schedule F (Form 1040), line 34;* or Schedule K-1 (Form 1065),* box 14, code A." Same candidate as the prior round (sum of sc.line31); the project changed with BUG-0176: person.sep_s1 now also refuses on person.se_screened. Checked against the source: the refusal covers the Schedule F and K-1 parts of Step 1 the tool does not take, and every item it refuses is already refused at Step 2 (person.se_line2 carries the same gate), so it removes a printed Step 1 that understated other self-employment income without refusing any return Step 2 did not; no finding. Project refusals: se_screened with a Schedule C (classm.asset.3, candidate $93,666.44, a refused return) and with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.ssb.5, classm.carloan.2, classm.f8959.1: candidate $0.00), plus the cited at-risk refusal; project-unknown records are persons with no Schedule C whose se_screen is not asked (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, candidate $0.00). In both no-Schedule-C groups Step 1 is not reached: person.s16 reads the plan deduction only with a Schedule C, and with a Schedule C person.se_line6 reads person.se_line2, so se_screen is always asked where the worksheet is used; kinds_by_return counts these on completed returns because the refusal or unknown stays local. The 2 candidate refusals are partials withholding se_screen where the candidate's sc.line31 refuses on other cited gates (classm.s179.4 s179.multi, classm.scveh.5 ho_both_limits). rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; p560 p. 39, Deduction Worksheet for Self-Employed, Step 2: "Enter your deduction for self-employment tax from Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15"; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE. Both copy this person's Schedule SE line 13; the differences are those of person.se_line13. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C (person.se_line2 is read by person.se_line6 only under person.has_sc) and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the self-employment items the screen lists (church employee income, clergy, partnership and farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (refused at person.credit). The candidate refusals (classm.carloan.2, classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The project refusal is the cited at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return"). rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C and otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c (i1040sse p. 2, line 4c; 'If less than $400 ... you don't owe self-employment tax'), which gives zero for the same person. Church employee income, optional methods, statutory employees and notaries are refused on both sides (person.se_screen, sc.statutory). Both then take one-half of the self-employment tax (Pub. 560 chapter 5, Deduction Worksheet for Self-Employed, step 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling). Box 1 is the same on both sides. Line 1e goes to the only person whose Forms W-2 show box 10, or to the taxpayer when nobody's do, on both sides; when both spouses' do, the second now gives it to neither (and refuses, its h_dc_1e_split), where the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6): shown in the taxpayer's line 4 and refused when a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate). The self-employment part is the same on returns the tool completes: the second subtracts the Schedule SE deduction without a Schedule C guard (zero below the $400 floor, so the Schedule C result is used, as the project does when no Schedule SE is filed) and leaves out statutory employee income, which is refused on each Schedule C (sc.statutory). i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Box 1 and the self-employment part are the same on both sides: the self-employment part differs only as person.eic_se does (the project's zero for a person with no Schedule C against the second's $400 floor, and the second's exclusion of statutory employee income, which is refused by sc.statutory), and both use Schedule C profit or loss when no Schedule SE is filed (p503 p. 11, Self-employment earnings, "Include your self-employment earnings in earned income, even if they are less than $400 and you didn't file Schedule SE"). Line 1e goes to the only person on a return that is not joint and to the one spouse whose Forms W-2 show box 10 on both sides. The sides differ only when both spouses' Forms W-2 show box 10: the second counts line 1e in both spouses' earned income, so it counts it twice; the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6), refusing when line 1e is above zero and a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate) and otherwise showing it in the taxpayer's line 4, where it cannot change the credit. i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

The candidate uses line 3 less line 13 when line 4a is $400 or more, else the Schedule C total; the project uses the same choice keyed on line 6 more than zero. Same value wherever both evaluate. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.json): 3,234 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 173 candidate-refuses, 1239 candidate-unknown, 1 project-refuses.

The new reply takes Schedule C line 31 less its own line 13 in every case; its note: "With no farm income and no optional method, Schedule SE line 3 equals Schedule C line 31, and line 13 is zero when no SE tax is owed." With farm income and optional methods refused (person.se_screen), Schedule SE line 3 is the Schedule C total and line 13 is zero below the $400 floor, so it equals the project's choice of Part 1 or Part 2; no value differs. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C (person.se_line2 is read by person.se_line6 only under person.has_sc) and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the self-employment items the screen lists (church employee income, clergy, partnership and farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (refused at person.credit). The candidate refusals (classm.carloan.2, classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The project refusal is the cited at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return"). rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. EIC Worksheet B Part 1 for a person filing Schedule SE and Part 2 otherwise on both sides (i1040gi p. 47).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. A distribution is refused on both sides (f8606.dist; the second's person.ira_dist_gate).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Where the second caps contributions at their limits (salary reductions at $16,500 and at compensation, catch-up at its limit and the compensation left after regular contributions), the project enters the contributions and refuses any amount above the limits (person.simple_excess: catch-up above person.catchup_max, employer contributions above person.employer_max, regular contributions above compensation; person.sep_excess; and the plan screen's 'contributions that are more than the maximum deductible amount'), so the caps never bind on a return the project admits; the second now also refuses excess SIMPLE contributions (its h_simple_excess) and takes the employer contribution uncapped, as the project does. The second's compensation, Schedule SE line 4a without the $400 floor of line 4c, is never below the project's (person.se_line4c), so it admits no less. The project also enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.has_sc), and asks person.plan only then; a person without a Schedule C is not self-employed in scope (partnership and farm income refused by scope.schedule1), and 'If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction' (i1040gi p. 93).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Where the second caps each contribution at its limit (the SEP at Step 21; SIMPLE employer contributions at the matching or 2% maximum, salary reductions at $16,500 and catch-up at its limit and compensation), the project enters the contributions and refuses any amount above the limits (person.sep_excess, person.simple_excess, and the plan screen's 'contributions that are more than the maximum deductible amount'), so the caps never bind on a return the project admits; the second's compensation, profit times 92.35% without the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, is never below the project's, so it admits no less. The project also enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.has_sc), and asks person.plan only then; a person without a Schedule C is not self-employed in scope (partnership and farm income refused by scope.schedule1), and 'If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction' (i1040gi p. 93). Evaluated stage14.simple.match_age50 ($19,662.30) and stage14.simple.nonelective_60 ($22,858.20): the second's formula gives the same amounts.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." Same expression as the prior round: the same Schedule SE computation (line 4c floor, lines 8a to 12, line 13 one-half). The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C (person.se_line2 is read by person.se_line6 only under person.has_sc) and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the self-employment items the screen lists (church employee income, clergy, partnership and farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (refused at person.credit). The candidate refusals (classm.carloan.2, classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The project refusal is the cited at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return"). The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C (person.se_line2 is read by person.se_line6 only under person.has_sc) and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta).
